title: Sweet Potato & Black Bean Enchiladas with Spinach, Melted Cheese & Lime-Cabbage Slaw
components_from_title: Sweet potato and black bean filling
summary: Baked enchiladas with tender sweet potato, black beans, spinach and kosher cheese, plus a bright crunchy cabbage slaw. 40–45 minutes total, 25–30 minutes active.
ingredients: 2 medium sweet potatoes (about 1 lb), peeled and cut into 1/2-inch cubes
1 can (15 oz) black beans, drained and rinsed
2 packed cups baby spinach, washed and checked as appropriate
8 small kosher-certified corn or flour tortillas
1 3/4 cups mild kosher-certified pareve red enchilada sauce
1 1/4 cups shredded kosher-certified cheddar or Monterey Jack cheese
2 cups shredded green or purple cabbage, checked as appropriate
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F. Boil diced sweet potatoes in lightly salted water for 8–10 minutes until just fork-tender; drain well.

While potatoes boil, heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a skillet. Sauté onion 3–4 minutes. Add cumin and paprika, then spinach and cook until wilted, about 1 minute. Fold in drained sweet potatoes and black beans; lightly mash a few cubes so the filling holds together.

Spread 1/2 cup mild enchilada sauce in a 9x13-inch baking dish. Fill each tortilla with about 1/3 cup filling and a pinch of cheese, roll, and arrange seam-side down. Pour remaining 1 1/4 cups sauce over the rolls and scatter the remaining cheese on top.
Bake uncovered for 14–17 minutes until filling is hot and cheese is melted and lightly bubbling. If using thick refrigerated sauce or cold filling, allow additional minutes until heated throughout.
While enchiladas bake, toss shredded cabbage and diced cucumber with lime juice, 1 tbsp olive oil, and a pinch of salt. Serve slaw on the side with optional avocado.
child_friendly_modifications: Use mild enchilada sauce and reserve 1–2 tortillas with very little sauce. Mash the sweet potato and beans slightly for a softer filling; cut enchiladas into bite-size pieces and serve slaw components separately. For a child who dislikes spinach, chop it finely or reserve some filling before adding it. Let melted cheese cool before serving.
leftovers: Refrigerate within 2 hours in shallow containers and eat within 3–4 days. Reheat covered in a 350°F oven or microwave until steaming hot (165°F). Store slaw separately and eat within 1–2 days for best crunch. Leftover filling can go into a warm cheese quesadilla for lunch.
